ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Diet and fracture healing: evidence-aware review: 4

A well-nourished patient plans to take very high doses of calcium and vitamins to force a fracture to heal faster. There is no documented deficiency. Which principle best addresses this proposed supplementation strategy?

  1. Adequate protein and micronutrient intake
  2. Appropriate mechanical stability
  3. Adequate blood supply
  4. Individualized medication review
  5. Avoid unsupported megadose supplementation
Answer and explanation

Avoid unsupported megadose supplementation

More vitamins or minerals than required are not established accelerators of fracture union and can cause harm.

Option explanations

Avoid unsupported megadose supplementation: More vitamins or minerals than required are not established accelerators of fracture union and can cause harm.

Adequate protein and micronutrient intake: Healing needs adequate nutrition; correcting deficiency is more defensible than promising benefit from excessive supplementation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Appropriate mechanical stability: Nutrition cannot compensate for inadequate fracture stability. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Adequate blood supply: Biological healing requires viable perfused tissue as well as mechanical support. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Individualized medication review: The risks and benefits of medicines during healing should be reviewed; prescribed drugs should not be stopped indiscriminately. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
